newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end stronger with U.S. on PPI data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end stronger with U.S. on PPI data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Wednesday, taking their cue from gains in U.S. treasuries, with markets in both countries benefiting from a tame U.S. producer price index report, analysts said.

"It was the strength we've seen in the U.S. tied to the soft PPI report this morning and the rumors of further progress in the budget deal. That's primarily driving Canadian markets," said Mark Chandler, senior economist with Goldman Sachs Canada.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.30 to C$110.90 to yield 7.074 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 15/32 to yield 6.89 percent. The spread between the bonds was 18 basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Tuesday.

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets strengthened this morning after the U.S. Labor Department reported that the producer price index fell 0.6 percent in April, compared with expectations that it would remain unchanged.

The report was seen as reducing the likelihood that the U.S. Federal Reserve would hike rates at next week's meeting of its Open Market Committee. A U.S. rate hike would likely weaken the Canadian bond market.

"We were at higher levels earlier today. We've come down from those highs as the currency has weakened off," said Chandler. "The U.S. dollar is under a lot of pressure and at least this time around it appears that it's spilling over into Canada," he said.
Analysts said Canadian financial markets are awaiting the release of the Bank of Canada's semi-annual monetary policy report on Thursday.
The report is expected to provide some clues on the central bank's intentions with regard to domestic interest rates and the currency.
Bond investors will also be closely examining consumer price index reports for April being released in both Canada and the United States on Thursday.

In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.23 to C$103.23 to yield 6.539 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 10/32 to yield 6.67 percent. The negative spread between the two bonds narrowed to 13 basis points from 15 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 3.08 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.17 percent.
